confirmed.title: Live supplier quotes will be rejected as 'not identical': tool reply says Goodbye after the first record_quote, and partNumberSaid is optional
confirmed.reason: The code does what the claim says. Whether the live demo fails depends on how Haiku behaves. In orchestrator.ts:406-416, partNumberSaid is `str(a.partNumberSaid) || undefined`. identicalPart is `parts.isIdentical(partNumberSaid, job.part)`. In parts.ts:106-108, isIdentical returns false when the number is empty. guards.checkQuote (guards.ts:159) then rejects with "could not confirm the identical part". usableQuotes (orchestrator.ts:277) filters on identicalPart, so a rejected quote is never usable. assistants.ts:75 requires only price and inStock, so partNumberSaid is optional in the schema. The prompt says to call record_quote "as soon as you have the price", before the read-back at the end. handleQuote always returns "...Goodbye." (line 445), which nudges the model to end the call. The sim always passes partNumberSaid (sim.ts:225), so it never exercises this path. A later call from the model would replace the first quote (filtered by callId). But the Goodbye reply makes that later call unlikely, and nothing in the code recovers from a missing number. Two things soften it. The prompt does tell the model to set partNumberSaid, and a model may fill it with the number it asked for, which would pass. So the failure is likely but not certain. The cost is high: the quote is rejected, there is no usable quote, and the job escalates, which breaks the demo. Suggested fix: treat an empty partNumberSaid as confirmed, and reject only a mismatched number.

confirmed.title: Live endCall likely never hangs up: no monitorPlan.controlEnabled, so controlUrl is missing and the fallback is DELETE /call (deletes call data)
confirmed.reason: The code matches the claim's main point. assemble() in server/src/vapi/assistants.ts (lines 146-161) never sets monitorPlan. grep finds no "monitor" anywhere in server/src outside client.ts, where createCall reads res.monitor?.controlUrl. As I recall, Vapi's monitorPlan.controlEnabled and listenEnabled both default to false, but I did not check this against the Vapi docs. In that case controlUrl will be undefined. endCall in server/src/vapi/client.ts (lines 78-95) then falls back to DELETE /call/:id. That is Vapi's "delete call data" endpoint, and the code's own comment says its effect on a live call is "UNVERIFIED". Errors are swallowed, so the kill switch reports success even if no call is hung up. endCall is used by stop(), the stuck check, straggler hang-up after best_deal, and reset, via dialer.endCall at orchestrator.ts lines 272, 305, 611 and 722. If the fallback does not hang up, live calls keep running until silenceTimeoutSeconds (15) or maxDurationSeconds ends them. The orchestrator's own state still moves on, so this is bounded and does not corrupt the accounting. The late record_quote part of the claim is speculative: I did not verify that handleQuote lacks a state check. The fix is a one-line addition of monitorPlan: { controlEnabled: true } to the assistant. I rate it medium, not high, because the damage is limited to calls that keep going after a stop or best_deal.

confirmed.title: Default FIXIE_MODEL 'claude-sonnet-5-5' is not in Vapi's verified Anthropic model list
confirmed.reason: The code matches the claim, but it is only a risk, because I could not confirm that Vapi rejects the name. server/src/config.ts:22, server/.env and server/.env.example all set FIXIE_MODEL to 'claude-sonnet-5-5'. assistants.ts:130 uses that value for the intake, user-callback and delivery lanes, and Haiku for the warranty, supplier and tech lanes. docs/review/vapi-api-facts.md F8 lists only claude-sonnet-5, claude-haiku-5-5, claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 and claude-opus-4-6, and says names not on that list are unverified. docs/review/SYNTHESIS.md:49 also names `claude-sonnet-5`. So the default departs from the reviewed, verified list, and nothing in the repo shows that Vapi accepts it. Vapi validates the Anthropic model name against a fixed list, so an unlisted name probably returns a 400 on assistant creation. If it does, the transient user and delivery assistants fail at call time, which would break the live callback and delivery legs. The intake assistant would probably fail earlier, at setup or boot PATCH, so that one is likely to show up before the demo. The failure chain depends on Vapi's real validation, but a wrong name here would break the live demo, and the fix is a one-line change to a verified name (claude-sonnet-5) in .env and the default. I rate it medium rather than high because the name may be valid, and the intake-lane failure would likely be visible at setup.

confirmed.title: savedVsNextBest compares against rejected or out-of-stock quotes, which can produce 'Beats X by $-12.00'
confirmed.reason: The code does what the claim says. At orchestrator.ts:314, `others` filters only on callId, identicalPart and vendorId. handleQuote (lines ~419-428) keeps rejected quotes in `job.quotes`, with `rejectedReason` set and `inStock` possibly false, and the guard does not drop them. `usableQuotes()` does exclude them, and `best` comes from it, so `best` and `others` use different pools. Take an identical-part quote from supplier B at $22 that is out of stock, and a quote from supplier A at $35 that is in stock. A becomes `best`, and B is `others[0]`. Then `savedVsNextBest` is 22-35 = -13, and the best_deal reason reads "Beats B by $-13.00". The metrics tile and the `savedVsNextBest` field carry the negative value too. Over-budget identical quotes are also included, so "Beats X" can name a supplier that was skipped. This is a display and metrics bug only. Ranking, the best pick and the call flow are unaffected. It matters on the live demo only when a cheaper supplier is out of stock and the identical-part flag is true, which is a plausible demo story and the sim already has an out_of_stock persona. The fix is a small change: build `others` from `usableQuotes(fresh)`. It is low severity, but worth fixing because the negative figure would be visible on screen.

confirmed.title: Kill switch or reset during dialing: a call whose createCall is in flight is placed after STOP and never ended
confirmed.reason:
The race exists in the code, but it is narrow, so I rate it low. In dialer.ts, placeGuardedCall awaits createWithRetry (POST /call) and only then calls calls.register. It never re-checks the epoch or the job state after the await. orchestrator.ts stop() snapshots calls.forJob(jobId) and ends only those calls, after moving the job to STOPPED. resetAll() snapshots calls.live() the same way. A createCall still in flight when either runs is therefore missed. Its call is registered afterwards as 'ringing' and call_started is emitted. Nothing ends it, and it runs until maxSec or until the callee hangs up. After a reset, jobs.update is a no-op, but emit still fires for the dead job.

Why the impact is limited: the window is only the POST /call latency, roughly 0.5 to 2 s. It applies only to calls dispatched in the startSourcing loop, which are staggered 300 ms apart, and a retry on a concurrency error adds a 5 s sleep to that window. The call is bounded by maxSec. A stray call is also unlikely to affect state, because webhook events for it hit the epoch check or the STOPPED guard. It would matter if the kill switch were pressed in the first second or two of sourcing. Tonight's demo might do exactly that, so it is a small but real live-demo risk. The proposed fix of checking the epoch and job state after createCall and ending the call is sound.

confirmed.title: Stuck guard (20s) and 45s supplier/warranty maxDuration will kill real calls before the quote
confirmed.reason: The stuck guard works as the claim describes, and 20 s is tight for a live call. The 45 s part of the claim is weak, and the fix is a config change rather than a code change. checkStuck in guards.ts ends any live warranty or supplier call with c.quoted false once 20 s have passed since liveAt. liveAt is set when Vapi reports in-progress (orchestrator.ts:643). A 5 s interval runs the check (orchestrator.ts:238), so the call ends at roughly 20-25 s. runStuckCheck then emits guard{stuck} and calls dialer.endCall. The default is 20 s (config.ts:33, SPEC §119). The supplier opener (prompts.ts:~79) has the AI read a part number spelled in chunks, then wait for the human to say "let me check", look up the price and answer. That plausibly takes 20-30 s before record_quote sets quoted, so a real, unscripted teammate can be hung up on. Sim calls produce a quote about 8 s after answer, which is why the sim run never hits this. The 45 s maxDuration is not a real risk. The stuck guard only applies before the quote, and once the quote is recorded the 45 s cap can at most cut the readback. The 20 s default is also deliberate. The review docs chose it so the stuck guard can fire inside a 3-minute demo, and raising it would weaken that showpiece. CAP_STUCK_SECONDS can already be set in the environment, so no code change is needed. Raise CAP_STUCK_SECONDS to about 30-35 and rehearse one live supplier call.

confirmed.title: Delivery lane uses silenceTimeoutSeconds 15, which ends the call while the customer physically installs the part
confirmed.reason:
The claim holds up in the code. `assemble()` in /root/.t3/projects/compiled/server/src/vapi/assistants.ts:157 hardcodes `silenceTimeoutSeconds: 15` for every lane, delivery included. The delivery prompt in /root/.t3/projects/compiled/server/src/vapi/prompts.ts:109-123 is a step-by-step install walkthrough. The assistant speaks a step and then waits while the customer physically does it. If the caller stays quiet for more than 15 s, Vapi ends the call with `silence-timed-out`. `webhook.ts:35` maps that to `timeout`.

On a delivery call, nothing in `orchestrator.ts` handles it. The only special handling at line 576 is for sourcing lanes. `install_progress` and `report_fix` then never fire, so the job does not reach FIXED. The spec (docs/SPEC.md line 175) says delivery stays live even in degraded mode, so the live demo exercises this path.

Two things reduce the severity. In a rehearsed 3-minute demo the presenter probably answers quickly, and I did not confirm whether Vapi's silence timer pauses during tool calls. I did not test the live path. The fix is cheap and low-risk: make `silenceTimeoutSeconds` per lane, with delivery at about 60 and the others unchanged or modestly higher.

confirmed.title: Tool-call parsing only handles function.arguments and arguments; misses a flat `parameters` shape and prefers the wrong list
confirmed.reason: The code does exhibit the gap. toolEntries (webhook.ts ~75-86) reads args only from `tc.function.arguments ?? tc.arguments`. It never reads `tc.parameters`. When toolCallList is present it also never consults toolWithToolCallList, so a flat {id,name,parameters} entry gives args={} and the fallback list is never used. Under that shape, start_job would get no model and record_quote would get no price. The facts doc (docs/review/vapi-api-facts.md) marks the nested function.arguments form as verified. But I recall Vapi's own docs and community examples showing toolCallList entries as flat {id,name,parameters}, and the live path has never run against real Vapi. The fix is a one-line `?? tc.parameters` plus merging toolWithToolCallList[].toolCall when args are empty. Severity is medium rather than high because the repo's own verified facts say the nested shape is what Vapi sends, so the demo may work as is. The defensive fix is nearly free for a tool-call failure that would break the live demo.

confirmed.title: Kill switch, spend stop, stuck-hangup all depend on an end-call path that likely does nothing in live mode
confirmed.reason: The code supports the claim. `assemble()` in assistants.ts never sets `monitorPlan`, and a grep for monitor/controlEnabled finds nothing outside client.ts and contracts.ts. As far as I recall Vapi's docs, `monitorPlan.controlEnabled` defaults to false, so `monitor.controlUrl` is probably not returned. I could not check this from the repo, because vapi-api-facts.md says nothing about it. client.ts itself labels the end-call path "UNVERIFIED". Without a `controlUrl`, `endCall` falls back to `DELETE /call/:id`, which Vapi documents as "Delete Call Data". Nothing in the repo confirms it hangs up a live call. There is also a real code flaw: if the `controlUrl` fetch throws or times out, the whole try block aborts and the DELETE fallback never runs. The catch only does `console.warn`, so the `endCall` error event emitted in dialer.ts never fires, and the UI can show a successful stop. Calls would then run until `maxDurationSeconds`. That backstop (45-480 s) caps the damage. SPEC.md also says the kill switch is shown only in Q&A. So I rate it medium, not blocker. The fix is cheap and should be done before tonight: add `monitorPlan:{controlEnabled:true}` to `assemble()`, split the try so the DELETE fallback still runs, and test one real kill during rehearsal.

confirmed.title: Calls whose createCall is in flight escape the kill switch and /demo/reset
confirmed.reason: The code confirms the race. placeGuardedCall (dialer.ts) awaits createWithRetry, and the retry can sleep 5 s on a concurrency error. After the await it registers the ctx and emits call_started without re-checking the job state or the epoch. In orchestrator.ts, stop() moves the job to STOPPED and ends only calls already in calls.forJob(), so a call whose createCall is still in flight is missed. resetAll() ends only calls.live() and bumps the epoch, so it misses in-flight calls too. startSourcing's loop checks job state only before each dial, so calls 2-4 already in flight when the operator presses stop are not blocked. Once an in-flight call resolves, the webhook ignores its events: onCallEvent returns early when the epoch is stale or the job is STOPPED. Nothing else ends the call. runStuckCheck only runs while the job is SOURCING. The call therefore runs until Vapi's maxDurationSeconds (set in assistants.ts) or silenceTimeoutSeconds (15 s), whichever comes first. The window is narrow, roughly the createCall latency of about 1 s, so the bug is real but intermittent. It matters for a live demo, because an operator pressing kill right after the first call_started could leave stray calls ringing a supplier. I rate it medium rather than high because the call is bounded by the max-duration and silence timeouts, and the window is small. The proposed fix is sound: after createCall resolves, re-check the job state and epoch, and end the call immediately if either has changed.

**Finding 1 (in-flight createCall escapes kill switch and /demo/reset): fixed, in `/root/.t3/projects/compiled/server/src/dialer.ts`.**

`dialer.ts` already had the epoch and job-state re-check after `createWithRetry` resolved (dead states: STOPPED, ESCALATED, FIXED, DECLINED, NOTIFIED). It ended the call and returned null without emitting `call_started`. The remaining gap was that it never settled the reservation. After a stop, the call's reserved minutes stayed in `job.reservedMinutes`. That is probably the cause of the minutes metric jump you saw.

My change:
- **State:** the ctx is marked `ended` before `endCallCtx`.
- **Settle:** when the epoch is unchanged and the job still exists, it calls `guards.settle(live, ctx, 0, 0)` followed by `jobs.update`. After a reset it skips the settle, because the job store is gone.
- **Registry:** I left out `calls.register` on purpose. Registering a late call after a reset would leak it into the cleared registry.

Not done: the optional per-job in-flight dial tracking so `stop()` could await in-flight dials. It would need changes in `orchestrator.ts`.

**Cross-file follow-up (optional):** a timed-out `POST /call` (the 15 s abort) can still create a Vapi call that nobody tracks. A fix would need `vapi/client.ts`, for example a lookup by call name.

I didn't investigate the 8.63 to 0.94 minutes drop beyond this settle gap.

Summary:
1. `npm run verify` reports 1 of 13 steps failed. The enterprise fault scenario fails because the tech call never emits `call_started` and is hung up silently. The server log shows `[sim] createCall sim_42 lane=tech`, then `sim_42 ended (assistant-ended-call)`, with no `call_started` event.
2. Root cause: `src/orchestrator.ts:342` calls `move(jobId,'SOURCING','NOTIFIED')` right after `dialer.placeGuardedCall` reserves, before `createCall` returns. Back in `src/dialer.ts:60`, `DEAD_STATES` includes `'NOTIFIED'`. When `createCall` resolves (the check is at about line 126), the job reads as dead, so the call is ended and `null` is returned.
3. This also breaks the live enterprise path. The enterprise tech call is the only lane that moves to NOTIFIED before its call is created, and real Vapi `createCall` takes longer, so the race is guaranteed. The consumer flow is unaffected, since only enterprise jobs reach NOTIFIED. I did not fix it because it is a source bug, not a harness or config issue. A likely minimal fix is to exempt the tech lane in the `DEAD_STATES` check in `src/dialer.ts`, or to move to NOTIFIED only after `placeGuardedCall` resolves.
4. The "minutes" drop from 8.63 to 0.94 is not a bug. It is reserve-then-settle accounting. While a call is in flight the metric counts the call's reserved max (the delivery call started at +7.8s and minutes jumped to 8.63 at +8.0s), then settles to the actual duration when the call ends (0.94 at +13.0s). `verify` prints a note saying the same.
5. A smaller sim oddity in the fault scenario: all three suppliers were rejected as `not_identical` because the sim quotes WP3392519 while the fault part is NOX-5WK97401. The scenario still passed its other checks, but it means the enterprise demo has no usable quote and no `best_deal`.
